title: Korean-Style Gochujang Grilled Pork Ribs
shortDescription: Pork spare ribs are coated with a gochujang, soy, garlic, and ginger marinade, then cooked over indirect heat and finished over direct heat.
culturalContext: This Korean-style gochujang rib draft is a contemporary adaptation rather than a claim of one canonical Korean rib preparation. Cut, pre-cooking, marinade, smoke, and tenderness preferences vary.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill

ingredients.preparation: membrane removed; cut into 2- or 3-bone sections

mixOrder: Whisk gochujang and soy sauce smooth.
Add rice syrup, pear, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil.
marinadeOrSeasoning.marinationVessel: Nonreactive covered container at or below 40°F / 4°C
marinadeOrSeasoning.maximumPracticalMarinationWarning: Do not exceed 12 hours without test-cook approval; salt and enzymes may affect texture.
marinadeOrSeasoning.reserveBeforeRawContactInstruction: Reserve any serving sauce before the marinade contacts raw meat.
marinadeOrSeasoning.rawContactDiscardOrReboilInstruction: Discard marinade that contacted raw meat; do not brush it onto cooked food.
substitutions: Use only verified gluten-free gochujang and tamari for a gluten-free adaptation.

instructions.heading: Prepare safely
instructions.action: Remove the membrane, portion the ribs on a dedicated board, refrigerate promptly, and wash hands.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sections are evenly sized with the membrane removed.
instructions.safetyNote: Raw pork juices must not contact cooked food, banchan, or serving sauce.

instructions.heading: Mix the marinade
instructions.action: Whisk the marinade until smooth and reserve any finishing portion before raw contact.
instructions.safetyNote: Reserve any serving sauce before raw-meat contact.

instructions.heading: Marinate under refrigeration
instructions.action: Coat ribs lightly, cover, and refrigerate for 4 hours.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Every piece has a thin, even coating.
instructions.safetyNote: Never marinate meat at room temperature.

instructions.heading: Preheat the grill
instructions.action: Preheat a clean outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill; establish the heat zones described below.
instructions.temperature: Indirect medium-low heat, then medium direct heat
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The grate is hot, clean, and lightly oiled.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use a fuel-burning grill indoors; follow electric-grill ventilation instructions.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Cook covered over indirect heat, turning periodically, until safely above 145°F / 63°C and approaching tender; finish briefly over direct heat with clean reserved sauce. Test cooking must establish the final tenderness endpoint.
instructions.temperature: Indirect medium-low heat, then medium direct heat
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Ribs are safely above 145°F / 63°C, browned, and test-cook-verified tender before the rest.
instructions.safetyNote: 145°F / 63°C plus a 3-minute rest is the whole-cut pork safety minimum; tenderness may require a higher endpoint determined in test cooking.

instructions.heading: Rest and serve
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean platter, apply only clean reserved sauce if used, and rest 3 minutes before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The meat has completed the stated rest on a clean platter.
instructions.safetyNote: Use clean utensils and do not return cooked meat to the raw-meat platter.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill with indirect medium-low and direct medium zones, or an approved electric grill capable of covered indirect-style cooking. Keep raw and cooked tools separate.
targetInternalTemperature: At least 145°F / 63°C plus a 3-minute rest for safety; test cooking must establish the higher tenderness endpoint before publication.
visualDonenessCues: Meat has drawn back slightly from bone ends
Surface is glazed and browned, not burned
Thermometer confirms the safety minimum and test cooking confirms tenderness
foodSafetyNotes: Keep ribs refrigerated at or below 40°F / 4°C.
Reserve finishing sauce before raw contact.
Meet at least 145°F / 63°C plus a 3-minute rest.
Do not use fuel-burning grills indoors.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify gochujang and soy sauce labels.

substitutions: Use only verified gluten-free gochujang and tamari for a gluten-free adaptation.
ingredientSourcing: Choose cold, meaty spare ribs with intact packaging and no off odor.
makeAhead: Mix marinade up to 2 days ahead; marinate ribs only within the stated range.
storage: Refrigerate cooked meat in a shallow covered container within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat only the needed portion to 165°F / 74°C until steaming; avoid repeated reheating.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers in rice bowls or lettuce wraps within the approved window.
servingSuggestions: Serve cut between bones with rice and fresh vegetables.

faq.question: Why is the tenderness endpoint unresolved?
faq.answer: The official safety minimum and the higher texture endpoint are different; test cooking must validate the equipment-specific result.

faq.question: Can raw marinade glaze the ribs?
faq.answer: No. Use only sauce reserved before raw-pork contact.

metaDescription: Grill Korean-style gochujang pork ribs with indirect heat, reserved glaze, thermometer verification, and an explicit test-cook tenderness gate.
sourcesAndEditorialNotes: The locked Korean-style gochujang rib concept is a contemporary editorial formulation requiring test-kitchen and Korean food-editor review.
